did_you_know.text: Did you know? Saul was from the family of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin. Kish is described as a “mighty man of valor,” meaning a man of status and ability.
Did you know? Saul is described as “a choice and handsome man,” and as taller than everyone else—“from his shoulders upward.”
Did you know? Saul’s journey to Samuel began with a simple family task: searching for the donkeys that Kish had lost.
Did you know? After searching several areas without finding the donkeys, Saul worried that his father would stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about them.
Did you know? The young man who was with Saul suggested giving the man of God a quarter shekel of silver, which he had with him, so that he would tell them which way to go.
Did you know? The chapter explains the difference between the terms “seer” and “prophet”: in the past, a prophet in Israel was called a “seer.”
Did you know? A festive meal was being held at the high place, and the people were waiting for Samuel because he was supposed to bless the sacrifice before they ate.
Did you know? Before Saul arrived, the LORD had revealed to Samuel that he would meet a man from Benjamin, anoint him as leader, and send him to save Israel from the Philistines.

Did you know? Samuel told Saul that the donkeys had been found, but immediately hinted that “all that is desirable in Israel” was connected with him and his father’s family—a hint of his future status.

Did you know? Samuel seated Saul at the head of the guests and ordered a special portion to be served to him, which the cook had set aside in advance, even though Saul still did not know why he was being honored in this way.
